entries.title: QatarEnergy extends LNG force majeure and charters out tankers into October, sources say
entries.claimSummary: QatarEnergy extended force majeure for LNG supplies to several Asian buyers into mid-September.
extractedFacts: Force-majeure notices due to expire in August and early September were extended until mid-September.
Affected buyers include customers in South Korea, India and Bangladesh.
QatarEnergy continued leasing some LNG tankers through mid-October.
At least nine QELM/QET-controlled LNG carriers were sub-chartered to named third parties.

entries.title: Strait of Hormuz Crossings Rise 8% Week-on-Week, But Dark AIS Activity Remains Elevated
entries.claimSummary: Kpler vessel-type data reported via Foreign Policy Journal shows 3 LNG tanker transits among 106 total Hormuz crossings during Jul 27-Aug 2, the first LNG-specific movement since the carried July 18 zero-transit observation.
extractedFacts: The week of Jul 27-Aug 2 recorded 106 total crossings by 96 distinct vessels, up 8% from 98 crossings the prior week.
Vessel-type breakdown of the 106 crossings included 3 LNG tankers, 40 liquid tankers, 24 bulk carriers, and smaller counts of other vessel types.
Dark AIS activity (undetermined routes) covered 41% of crossings, down from 49% the prior week.
